solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some in the audience sit up, edgily backing substitute

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the run picked out is read from right to left
only some of the letters in this stretch of the audience are taken, the run sitting inside the words

explanation.surface: A theatre audience shifts nervously in their seats while an understudy waits to step in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some in' picks ESITUPED from 'audience sit up, edgily', and 'backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to act as a stand-in for someone, so the verb substitute fits.

clue.text: Track down uprising in Wilts

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the letters from bottom to top, so the pieces come out backwards

parts.note: a spoor is the track or trail of an animal

explanation.surface: Following a trail to a rebellion in Wiltshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Wilts is also short for Wiltshire, an English county, which makes the surface read as a place; here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that wilts sags and flops, the same as one that hangs limply.

clue.text: 7's work helped town after disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in chaos, so these three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lent a hand to a town recovering from a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is the composer at 7-down, Prokofiev; 'disaster' scrambles HELPED TOWN AFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Prokofiev wrote this musical tale for children, with a narrator and orchestra.

clue.text: 2's gunfire ends around noon

indicators.note: around means the word for ends is wrapped about the letter for noon

parts.note: tips are the ends of things, such as fingertips
M stands for meridies, Latin for noon, as in a.m. and p.m.

explanation.surface: Shots ring out at the stroke of midday in a battle scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In Peter and the Wolf (2-down) the hunters' gunshots are played on the kettledrums.
explanation.definitionFit: Timps is musicians' slang for timpani, the drums that sound the hunters' shots in the piece.

clue.text: 2's hero has stone jewellery

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight
rings are items of jewellery

explanation.surface: A storybook hero owns a precious gem among his jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter, the hero of 2-down, is played by the orchestra's string section.
explanation.definitionFit: Each character in the tale has an instrument, and the boy Peter's theme belongs to violins, violas, cellos and basses.

clue.text: Time in army unit is a constant equilibrium

indicators.note: in places the letter for time inside the regiment's initials

parts.note: the SAS (Special Air Service) is a British army regiment
taken as written

explanation.surface: Waiting time in a regiment is a state of never-ending balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a condition of inactivity or balance in which nothing changes.

clue.text: Swan necessary for 2's hunters

definitions.meaning: the ... swan is a large North American swan with a bugling call
a player of a brass instrument who might be required to sound the hunting party's music in Prokofiev's tale

explanation.walkthrough: 2 is Peter and the Wolf, at 2-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter is both a species of swan and a brass player in an orchestra.

clue.text: Forgive porkies spread about European composer

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the letter for European
spread means the letters of these two words are scattered and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A plea to pardon the lies being told about someone from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges FORGIVE PORKIES, and 'about' sets that round E. Porkies is British rhyming slang for lies (pork pies).
explanation.definitionFit: Prokofiev was a twentieth-century Russian writer of symphonies, ballets and operas.

clue.text: Among fancied teams, university cricket club does well

indicators.note: among means the next pieces are placed in the middle of the word for fancied teams

parts.note: seeds are the teams or players ranked as favourites in a tournament

explanation.surface: A college cricket side holds its own against the favourites.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed is to achieve your aim, in other words to do well.

clue.text: Where French prostitute entertains Sergeant-Major Fox

parts.note: the French for where is ou

indicators.note: entertains means the word for prostitute takes the next piece in, as a host takes a guest

parts.note: tart is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A seedy scene in France in which a soldier called Fox is the client.
explanation.walkthrough: Fox looks like a name; it is a verb, to fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To fox someone is to baffle or trick them, getting the better of them by cunning.

clue.text: Copper's trophy the last in order, I see

parts.note: a cup is a trophy

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word order is the one taken

parts.note: I see read as letters is IC, the I followed by a C that sounds like see

explanation.surface: A policeman's trophy is the last in line, I see.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a policeman; it is the metal, and the possessive stands for an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupric is the chemistry adjective for compounds of copper, from Latin cuprum.

clue.text: 2's villain with no hair after losing head

indicators.note: the word must drop its first letter, the head of the word

parts.note: shorn means with the hair or fleece cut off

explanation.surface: A bald baddie in a story who has also been beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: The wolf in 2-down is played by three French horns.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolf, the tale's menace, has his theme given to the brass instruments of that name.

clue.text: Places to play piano on ships

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
an ark is a ship, as in Noah's

explanation.surface: Somewhere aboard ocean liners where a pianist can perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Parks are public open spaces where children go out for games.

clue.text: Back shortly with priest present for Teilhard de Chardin's human intelligence and memory

definitions.text: Teilhard de Chardin's human intelligence and memory

indicators.note: back means the word for shortly is turned round

parts.note: soon means shortly, before long
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A priest returns and is on hand to discuss a French Jesuit thinker's idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre Teilhard de Chardin was a Jesuit philosopher who popularised this term.
explanation.definitionFit: The noosphere is his name for the realm of collective human thought, from Greek noos, mind.

clue.text: Pants and comes back to life?

definitions.meaning: pants in the British sense of underpants
read playfully as ..., the reverse of dies

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up verb: if dying is undone, someone un-dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Undies is an informal word for underwear, and the joke reading undoes a death.

clue.text: Under evaluation at home, electronic digestion mechanism

parts.note: something being evaluated is in test
in means at home
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A digestive gadget is being tested by someone at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The intestine is the long tube of the gut where food is broken down and absorbed.

clue.text: A top-end collection of papers stuck together

indicators.note: a collection gathers the letters up and puts them together in another order

explanation.surface: An upmarket set of documents glued into one bundle.
explanation.definitionFit: A notepad is a block of writing sheets gummed along one edge.

clue.text: New article about 2's cat

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A fresh newspaper piece about a cat in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat in 2-down is played by the clarinet; 'about' rearranges N plus ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Each animal in the tale has its own instrument, and the slinking cat's theme is on this woodwind.

clue.text: Decide not to punish bird seen among bricks

indicators.note: the bird is seen in the middle of the bricks, so its word goes inside

parts.note: Lego is the brand of toy building bricks
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A bird spotted in a pile of bricks escapes a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: To let it go is an idiom for overlooking an offence instead of punishing it.

clue.text: Empty award for 2's duck

indicators.note: read loosely, the award is taken with nothing put in place inside it, so the letter for empty goes within

parts.note: the OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour
empty gives O, the zero-shaped letter for nothing

explanation.surface: A hollow honour handed to a storybook duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The award is read as empty, holding O (nothing) inside OBE; 'for' does the placing. The duck in 2-down is played by the oboe.
explanation.definitionFit: The waddling duck's theme in Prokofiev's piece is given to this double-reed instrument.

clue.text: Start buying weapon for Clyde?

indicators.note: the start of the word buying is its opening letter

parts.note: an arrow is a weapon shot from a bow

explanation.surface: Purchasing a weapon for someone named Clyde.
explanation.walkthrough: Clyde looks like the Scottish river; the question mark points to a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Clyde Barrow was the American outlaw partnered with Bonnie Parker in the 1930s.

clue.text: Fool in favour of 2's grandfather

indicators.note: in means the word for fool sits inside the word for favour

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot backs the old man in the story.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter's grumpy grandfather in 2-down is played by the bassoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The grandfather's gruff theme is given to this low woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Cat is one writer's obsessed about

indicators.note: about means the word for obsessed goes around the next piece

parts.note: anal, short for anal-retentive, means obsessively fussy
the writer's is I'm, the writer is

explanation.surface: A writer confesses to an obsession with a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is an example of a creature of the kingdom of beasts.

clue.text: Pressed to repair organ parts

indicators.note: to repair is to put back together, so the letters are reassembled into another order

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to fix a church instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Reed stops are pipe-organ controls bringing in pipes that sound by a vibrating reed.

clue.text: Force 50 have escaped

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Fifty people under duress have broken free.
explanation.definitionFit: As in the bird has flown, flown means fled or got away.

clue.text: Oddly fill up the bird in 2

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third, fifth and so on, are the ones taken

explanation.surface: A strange instruction to feed the bird in the story.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird in 2-down is played by the flute.
explanation.definitionFit: The chirping little bird's theme in Prokofiev's tale is played on this high woodwind.

clue.text: Without authorisation? That's it!

parts.note: no means without, as in no money
OK is approval or authorisation
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone acting without permission is told: that's it, you're done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' looks like a closing exclamation; it is the definition, slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Nookie is jocular British slang for sexual intercourse, which it also means informally.

clue.text: Bus to Lima nearly crashes, which makes people sick

indicators.note: a crash wrecks the vehicle and the letters are tumbled into a new order
nearly means the last letter of Lima is dropped

explanation.surface: A coach heading to the Peruvian capital almost has an accident, causing nausea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts Lima to LIM, and 'crashes' rearranges BUS TO LIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Botulism is a serious food poisoning caused by a bacterial toxin.

clue.text: Sweet scent of feeding bottles

indicators.note: bottles is a verb here: the words hold the letters inside them as a bottle holds liquid

explanation.surface: Baby bottles giving off a sugary smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like the plural noun; it is the verb that holds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection of boiled sugar and butter.

clue.text: Break in travel at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Taking a pause during a voyage by ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a pause or intermission between parts of a performance.
